title: Legislative districts of Romblon

{{Short description|Legislative districts in the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Romblon''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Romblon]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{See also|Legislative districts of Capiz}} Romblon, then part of the province of [[Capiz]], initially had two delegates, appointed at-large, to the [[Malolos Congress]] in [[1898 Philippine legislative election|1898]]; this remained so until 1899. Romblon was represented as part of the [[Capiz's 3rd congressional district|third district]] of Capiz from 1907 to 1919. It was later reestablished as a separate province in 1917,{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=2724|title=An Act authorizing the separation of the SubProvince of Romblon from the province of Capiz and the reestablishment of the former province of Romblon, and for other purposes|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l837e|date=December 7, 1917|accessdate=January 12, 2023}} thus its separate representation was restored, electing one representative this time in [[1919 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1919]]. Romblon was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned one representative, elected at large, to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. ==List of Lone District Representatives== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; width:40%;" |- ! width="40%"| Period !
